title: CmdPal: Low-level keyboard hook toggle description is inversed

judgment.rationale: The issue is a wording-only defect with confirmed runtime semantics and exact resource ownership.
evidence: The setting text claims low-level hook mode fixes elevated-app activation.
WH_KEYBOARD_LL cannot observe higher-integrity input from a non-elevated process.
The setting only selects KeyboardListener versus RegisterHotKey; runtime behavior need not change.

fix_assessment.rationale: No existing fix attempt corrects the misleading setting description.

proposed_fixes.title: Correct the CmdPal low-level hook explanation
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The English resource string describes the elevated-app limitation as the reason to enable the hook, reversing the actual tradeoff.
plan: Update the English resource to describe reserved shortcut support and the elevated-process limitation.
Keep SettingsViewModel, hotkey selection, persistence, and localization mechanics unchanged.
Validate the text in the General settings page and confirm toggling still changes modes.
verification: The description no longer promises elevated-app activation and the existing setting behavior remains unchanged.

confidence.rationale: The resource string and the two runtime branches are directly identified in source.

issue_context.summary: CmdPal's low-level keyboard hook setting has inverted explanatory text; the setting's implementation is not itself implicated.
known_information: The issue targets the Command Palette settings page.
The current text says to use the hook when activation from an elevated app fails.
KeyboardListener uses WH_KEYBOARD_LL while the alternate path uses RegisterHotKey.
The report links the integrity-level reason for the observed behavior.
inferences: The copy should mention reserved Windows shortcuts while avoiding an absolute guarantee for elevated apps.
issue_context.analysis: The setting's persisted flag and runtime mode selection are already coherent. Correcting only the English description prevents a misleading expectation without changing hotkey behavior.
initial_investigation: Inspected GeneralPage.xaml, SettingsViewModel, MainWindow setup, KeyboardListener, and the en-us resource.
Reviewed related activation issues and git history; they concern capability behavior rather than this copy defect.
Fork mirror Issue 641 contains the detailed design and adversary approval.

design.root_cause: Settings_GeneralPage_LowLevelHook_SettingsCard.Description says the hook helps activation from elevated apps, but WH_KEYBOARD_LL is subject to integrity-level restrictions and the hook is intended for shortcuts intercepted or reserved by Windows.
evidence: [Observed] The resource string contains the inverted elevated-app claim.
[Observed] SetupHotkey selects KeyboardListener when enabled and RegisterHotKey otherwise.
[Inferred] No code change is required for this issue.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: The description implies enabling the hook remedies elevated-app focus.
implementation_steps.change: Explain that the hook can help with Windows-reserved shortcuts but may not work while an elevated app is focused unless PowerToys is also elevated.
implementation_steps.code_block: - Use this if the shortcut cannot focus Command Palette from an elevated app\n+ Use this for shortcuts reserved by Windows, such as Win plus Space. It may not work while an elevated app is focused unless PowerToys is running as administrator.
edge_cases: Keep the wording short enough for the existing settings card.
Update translations through the normal localization process; do not alter runtime bindings.
tests: Confirm toggling still switches between KeyboardListener and RegisterHotKey.

verify: Build the CmdPal UI project with the repository's existing build script.
Open CmdPal settings and verify the corrected description.
Test a reserved shortcut and an elevated-app focus case to ensure the text matches behavior.
risks: Users may find integrity terminology technical; use plain elevated-app wording.
Translations will lag until the localization workflow updates them.
alternatives: Adding a runtime warning is broader than this copy issue.
Changing hook mechanics would not address the inverted text.
